subject: Hosting path quick recap & migration risks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jung <claire@atlashealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next info we need (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Claire — thanks again for taking time today. Wanted to capture a short post-call recap and a list of clarifying items so we can put a concrete pilot proposal in front of procurement.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goals: reduce per-token inference costs for customer-facing product, keep 95th pct latency under 350ms, and ensure PHI residency for a subset of flows.
- Current footprint: production traffic on OpenAI for most features, plus an internal GPU cluster for a small set of custom models.
- Deployment preference: you said Atlas is leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput but may need a Private/VPC option for PHI in regulated workflows. Hosted API looked attractive for early velocity.

Key questions for us to size options (could you confirm):
1) Median qps and top-of-day peak qps for text generation and embeddings? (approx numbers are fine)
2) Which model families are in active use and which require on-prem weights (if any)?
3) Data residency constraints (which workflows must stay in VPC/on-prem vs can go to hosted)?
4) Any hard SLA or certification needs beyond SOC 2 Type II (e.g., HIPAA BAA, FedRAMP)?
5) Timeline and pilot budget for Proof-of-Concept (POC) or pilot (typical pilots are 4–8 weeks).

Attachments: redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf (high-level tradeoffs), migration-checklist.xlsx (info we need for migration plan).

Proposed immediate next steps
- If you can reply with the five items above, we’ll draft a two-track recommendation (Fast pilot on Hosted + Dedicated pilot plan; Dedicated/Private sizing for long-term).
- If procurement wants budgetary numbers we can include a rough committed capacity vs burst cost sketch.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min technical sync if you’d like to bring your infra lead.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Claire Jung <claire@atlashealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next info we need (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Marcus — thanks, this is helpful. Answers inline below.

1) Traffic: steady-state generation ~18 qps, embeddings calls ~6 qps. Peaks (end of month/feature launches) up to ~90 qps for generation for ~10–15 minutes bursts.
2) Models: production uses a mixture — mostly an API provider for base models (safety-tuned), and we run Llama2-derived custom finetunes on our in-house GPU cluster for specialty clinical summarization. Those finetuned weights cannot leave our environment today due to licensing/policy.
3) Residency: any workflow that touches PHI must remain within our VPC or on-prem environment. Non-PHI flows are fine to run on hosted.
4) Compliance: SOC 2 is required; HIPAA applicability — we’ll need a BAA for PHI flows.
5) Timeline/budget: we’re aiming for a 6–8 week pilot starting late July, procurement is comfortable with an initial budget band but will expect a clear mutual action plan and pilot scope.

Please include whether Redwood can support a hybrid approach (dedicated capacity for most traffic + private option for PHI flows) and what migration effort looks like for our in-house Llama2 finetunes.

—Claire
Claire Jung
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas Health
claire@atlashealth.com

(Procurement looped in for budget/contract items)

Can you propose two concrete options we can present to procurement:
A) Fast pilot: Hosted API + Dedicated burst path (low engineering lift, fastest time-to-value) — include cost estimate and what we need to prove in a 4-week pilot.
B) Long-term: Dedicated capacity with private VPC peering and a Private on-prem option for PHI-only flows (more work but meets residency & BAA).

Specific technical questions to answer in the proposal:
- Can Redwood Private import/run their finetuned Llama-derived weights without violating licensing? (we may need legal to confirm, but note any runtime constraints)
- Migration steps from their legacy GPU cluster: model format compatibility, tokenizer parity, KV cache warm-up, and quantization considerations.
- Recommended rollout pattern (can we do canary for PHI flows?).

Attachments from initial email are included. I’ll schedule a 30-min tech workshop after you draft the two options.

—Marcus

Subject: RE: Quick recap + next info we need (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — proposal options and migration checklist

Hi all — thanks for the clear answers, Claire. Below is a concise set of proposed options plus a migration checklist and next steps. I kept the language non-legal; procurement will need the SOW/BAA language later.

Option 1 — Rapid pilot (4 weeks)
- Architecture: Hosted API for non-PHI flows + Dedicated reserved capacity for production traffic (no VPC requirement for pilot).
- Why: very low engineering lift, fastest to validate latency/cost targets.
- What we’ll prove: end-to-end latency under load, token cost delta vs current provider, embedding parity.
- Requirements from Atlas: sample traffic replay, list of API calls to mirror, a test dataset (non-PHI) for accuracy/regression checks.
- Estimated effort: 2 weeks infra setup + 2 weeks validation.

Option 2 — Hybrid production (recommended if PHI is material)
- Architecture: Dedicated capacity in a customer-dedicated tenancy with Private VPC peering for PHI flows. For models that cannot leave Atlas, Redwood Private (on-prem appliance) or an agent-based approach that keeps weights local and routes requests through the private control plane.
- Why: meets residency and BAA needs while giving cost predictability.
- Migration considerations: model format conversion (we support PyTorch/ONNX imports), tokenizer parity check, KV cache warm-up strategy, and a short quantization evaluation (4-bit/8-bit) for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Data plane options: VPC peering (recommended) or customer-managed VPN if peering not allowed.

Migration checklist (high level)
- Inventory of models (file names, formats, sizes) and any license restrictions.
- Tokenizer artifacts and sample outputs for parity testing.
- A small representative test corpus (non-PHI) for quality/regression checks.
- Access plan for benchmarking (SFTP or secure transfer for artifacts) and a temporary test VM in your VPC for performance runs.
- Security review: SOC 2 evidence (we can share), BAA template for legal.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll create a mutual action plan doc (HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/AH-4392) and a 4-week pilot SOW draft.
2) Schedule a technical workshop (30–60 min) to walk infra + ML engineering through model import and a quick bench.
3) Procurement and legal — we’ll follow up with a BAA and a draft SOW for the pilot.

Notes on their Llama2 finetunes: we can run customer-provided finetuned weights in Redwood Private or in a private on-prem worker so long as licensing allows. If weights cannot leave their environment, the recommended pattern is to place inference workers in their VPC or on-prem and use a private control plane for orchestration.

I attached a short migration-checklist.xlsx and a hosting-comparison PDF (same files Marcus shared). I’ll prepare a short two-page pricing sketch for both options and share by EOD.

If that works, Marcus — I’ll coordinate dates for the workshop and draft the MAP. Claire — are mornings PST early next week reasonable for the technical workshop?

Best,
